Add the dictionary entries a pipeline reads to its targets

Source: R/targets.R
tar_dict_deps.Rd

tar_dict_deps() finds, in the command of each target and in the functions it calls from the pipeline's environment, the entries of the dictionary it reads (dict$key, dict[["key"]]; any other use of dict counts as reading every entry), and adds dict_<key> to the target's dependencies (rule 4.6.2). A target made by tarchetypes::tar_quarto() or tarchetypes::tar_render() is read the same way through its source files: chunk code, inline R and the code of constructs, included files too (rule 4.6.5). Includes rooted at / resolve against the Quarto project root. A report with a child= or include that the scan cannot resolve to a file (a computed path) depends on every key. A key that the dictionary does not hold is an error that lists every target that reads one (rule 4.6.4).

Usage

tar_dict_deps(targets, path = "dict.yml")

Arguments

targets

A target object, or a list of target objects and lists, nested to any depth.

path

The dictionary file, as given to tar_dict().

Value

targets, in the same structure. The target objects are changed in place, with the hooks of tarchetypes, which this function needs.

Details

See tar_dict() for the limit with crew workers: the dictionary is not visible to a parallel worker.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
weft::tar_dict_deps(list(targets::tar_target(t, dict$limit + 1)))
} # }
